_readme: Single source of truth for firm details. Every shared component, every page template and the structured-data generator read from here — nothing about the firm is written into a page by hand. scripts/check-placeholders.mjs reports anything still outstanding and fails a production build with --strict.
_firm: `firm` is the public name used in running copy. `firmLegalName` is the registered entity and is what appears in firm identification, legal pages, the copyright line and structured data. Florida Probation Law is the name of this website, not a law firm — never write it as one.
_basePath: Sub-directory the site is served from, or "" for a site at a domain root. It is empty because the site is served from floridaprobationlaw.com, where the files sit directly in public_html — so /css/styles.css is the correct path. Setting it wrongly is the one configuration mistake that breaks a deploy completely rather than partially: every internal href and src gets the prefix, the stylesheet 404s along with everything else, and the site renders as unstyled HTML. Only set it back to a path like "/repo-name" for a GitHub Pages *project* site, which serves from <user>.github.io/<repo>/. Can be overridden per build with BASE_PATH=... npm run build. Canonical and og:url are absolute and always use `url` above, so a preview never canonicalises to itself.
disclosure: FloridaProbationLaw.com is operated by Hoffman Legal, PLLC, a Florida law firm.
disclosureLong: FloridaProbationLaw.com is a legal information and legal services website operated by Hoffman Legal, PLLC.
_formEndpoint: Formspree project endpoint. All three intake forms POST here. Two consequences to keep in view: prospective-client details now pass through a third-party processor before reaching the firm, which is why /privacy-policy/ names Formspree — the policy must stay accurate if the endpoint ever changes; and Formspree's free tier caps submissions per month, after which further enquiries are rejected rather than queued. Setting this back to "" replaces the submit control with a visible notice giving the phone number and email, rather than a button that silently discards a case description.
_formRedirect: Where a successful submission lands. `formRedirectField` is the parameter name the endpoint reads — `_next` is what Formspree and Basin use. The value is written as an absolute URL built from `url` above, which is right for production; on a preview deploy js/main.js rewrites it to the origin actually being browsed, so a test submission does not bounce the visitor to a domain that is not live yet. With JavaScript off, the build-time production URL stands.

analytics._analytics: Clearing measurementId removes the tag from every page and turns every event call into a no-op — js/main.js checks for gtag before firing, so nothing breaks when the tag is absent, blocked, or still loading. Two things this brings that were not true before: the site now loads a third-party script and sets cookies (_ga and _ga_<id>), which is why /privacy-policy/ names Google Analytics and describes what it stores. Keep that page in step with this field. No event carries a form value, a name, a phone number, an email address or any case detail — only which form, on which page. Sending personal information to Analytics breaches Google's terms and, on an attorney intake form, would put prospective-client information somewhere it has no business being.

_formSpam: `_gotcha` is the field name Formspree filters on server-side, so naming the honeypot that gets spam handling the client cannot provide — a bot posting directly to the endpoint never runs js/main.js. `_subject` sets the notification subject line so enquiries are identifiable in the inbox.

attorney.name: David Hoffman
attorney.title: Attorney and Lead Counsel
attorney.imageAlt: Attorney David Hoffman of Hoffman Legal
attorney._image: TODO: Replace the temporary remote attorney image with a locally hosted optimized copy before final production deployment. It is served from another site the firm operates, which means an outbound dependency on a host this repository does not control — if that URL moves, the attorney page loses its photograph. Nothing else on this site loads a remote asset.
attorney._credentials: Only what has been supplied appears here. No law school, graduation year, honours, certification, membership or years-in-practice figure is recorded, because none was provided — and an unverifiable credential on a law firm site is a Fla. Bar Rule 4-7.13 problem, not a gap in the copy.

office._office: The firm's single bona fide office, satisfying Fla. Bar Rule 4-7.12. Written identically everywhere it appears. There is exactly one office: county pages describe a place the firm practises in, never a location it occupies.

availability.summary: Free initial consultations. Telephone enquiries accepted 24/7.
availability._availability: Phone intake is 24/7; the office itself is not, and no office-opening hours have been supplied, so none are published or emitted as openingHours structured data. Availability is never phrased as a promise of response time.

serviceArea.statement: Hoffman Legal is based in Dania Beach and primarily serves Broward, Miami-Dade and Palm Beach counties. Representation may be available throughout Florida depending on the matter.
serviceArea.outsidePrimary: Hoffman Legal does not maintain an office in this county. Representation may be available depending on the location, facts and procedural requirements of the case.

_servedCounties: County slugs inside the primary service area. These drive the areaServed values on the single organisation node in the schema graph. County pages outside this list carry the `serviceArea.outsidePrimary` statement instead. No county page emits an organisation, a LocalBusiness or an address of its own — there is one firm at one address.

bar.admission: Licensed to practice law in the State of Florida
bar._bar: Jurisdiction statement only. No registration identifier is recorded here by instruction.
